headline: Monash Council in Melbourne has refused Centuria's plan for a 38-megawatt data centre, overruling its own planning officers.
score_reason: Pool 5 lowered by 1: the vote was on 29 Sep 2026, six days before this report.
importance_line: Neighbours of the Clayton site and other developers in Victoria are affected, but the refusal may be appealed and the state's new rules are not yet in force.
summary: W.Media reports that Monash Council voted on 29 Sep 2026 to reject Centuria's AU$137 million, 38-megawatt data centre at Clayton, a Melbourne suburb, against the advice of its planning officers, citing the size of the expansion, its electricity needs and effects on nearby residents. Two councillors also pointed to Victoria's new Sustainable Data Centre Action Plan, including a proposed 150-metre gap from homes, although those rules are not yet in force.
notes: W.Media reports Centuria's options remain open.
